98a574177c.q: What inspired Gary Poyer to write Make Retiring Easy and how did he develop his retirement planning approach?
98a574177c.a: As a certified financial planner, Gary discovered that most of his clients did not have real plans for retirement beyond saving money. He investigated how to help them by exploring the personal growth industry and found life principles he could apply to retirement planning. This led him to leave RBC, create a workshop to help people develop a vision and retirement life plan, and eventually write Make Retiring Easy, designed as a template for financial advisors to help their clients.
98a574177c.e: The Interesting People You Meeting: Episode 44 "Insights From a Retirement Expert"

53e70e24c4.q: What is Gary Poyer's approach to helping retirement clients define their retirement vision when they don't know where to start?
53e70e24c4.a: Gary uses a timeline exercise where clients mark their date of birth, today's date, desired retirement date, and 20 years into retirement. He then has them define their retirement vision using three to five adjectives. Once they know their vision, he works with them to identify what activities align with that vision by looking at retirement as a time of opportunity, exploring options from relaxation to starting new businesses, reinventing themselves, and deepening personal relationships.
53e70e24c4.e: The Interesting People You Meeting: Episode 44 "Insights From a Retirement Expert"

30770a33a8.q: According to Gary Poyer, what is a major misconception about retirement planning that financial advisors often make?
30770a33a8.a: Many financial advisors tell clients not to worry about what they will do in retirement and to figure it out when they retire. Gary takes the opposite view, believing retirement brings a sense of urgency. He states clients should know exactly what they will do on their first day of retirement and what they want to accomplish in the first three to five years, because people procrastinate, years go by quickly, and lost time cannot be regained.
30770a33a8.e: The Interesting People You Meeting: Episode 44 "Insights From a Retirement Expert"

24746e55b4.q: What does Gary Poyer mean by saying retirement offers a world of potential and how can retirees access it?
24746e55b4.a: Many people don't see retirement as offering potential because they think only from their own life experiences and comfort zone. Gary encourages people to go beyond their comfort zone by reflecting on opportunities they took advantage of and those they missed. He recommends reading books, attending workshops, talking to financial advisors, and being proactive in asking people how they use their time in retirement to realize that retirement is the final frontier offering significant opportunity if people are willing to seek it out.
24746e55b4.e: The Interesting People You Meeting: Episode 44 "Insights From a Retirement Expert"

18731176b5.q: How does Gary Poyer use life purpose exercises to help business owners and professionals transition into retirement?
18731176b5.a: Many business owners and professionals identify themselves with what they do, so when they leave their profession they face an identity loss. Gary conducts a life purpose exercise to help them understand that just because they were a lawyer or business owner for 40 years does not mean they have to remain defined by that role. Their life purpose can evolve, and they can discover a new purpose even if they haven't previously identified one, giving them direction and preventing the sense of being lost.
18731176b5.e: The Interesting People You Meeting: Episode 44 "Insights From a Retirement Expert"

cce9124b9e.q: What is Gary Poyer's position on leaving a personal legacy versus a financial legacy in retirement?
cce9124b9e.a: Gary believes a personal legacy is even better than a financial legacy. While many clients want to leave money for children or grandchildren, recording your own life story—whether as video, recording, or handwritten—creates a personal legacy that generations from now will read and be amazed by, similar to how people today appreciate stories of historical figures like Ben Franklin or Canadian prime ministers.
cce9124b9e.e: The Interesting People You Meeting: Episode 44 "Insights From a Retirement Expert"
